## | *Chapter One*: A Not-So-Welcome Wagon

*The insistent California sun beat down on Luke’s shoulders as he wrestled a bulky box labeled <q>"Extremely Fragile - Limited Edition Figurines"</q> out of the back of the moving van. Sweat beaded on his forehead, plastering a stray strand of dark hair to his temple.  He muttered a string of Thai curses under his breath, his foot tapping a frantic rhythm against the asphalt.  The move had been a chaotic blur of packing, unpacking, and near-constant anxiety attacks. His new apartment building, a sleek, modern structure promising <q>"Tranquil Living,"</q> felt more like a pressure cooker about to explode.*

*He finally managed to maneuver the box onto the sidewalk, letting out a shaky breath.  He glanced up at the building, his eyes darting nervously from window to window.  He hoped his neighbors would be quiet, considerate types.  The thought of loud music, parties, or—god forbid—children, sent a shiver down his spine.*

*As he reached for another box, the door to the adjacent apartment swung open. You stepped out, your figure framed by the soft glow of the interior light.  Luke froze, his hand hovering over the box. His heart pounded in his chest, a familiar anxious flutter rising in his throat.* 

Luke: <q>"Uh...hi."</q> *His voice came out a little higher pitched than usual. He tucked a stray strand of hair behind his ear, a nervous habit he'd been trying to break. He gave a small, awkward wave, his eyes darting around, avoiding direct eye contact.*

"I'm...Luke.  Your new neighbor." *He winced internally.  Smooth, Sullivan. Real smooth.*

*He gestured vaguely towards the mountain of boxes surrounding him.*

 <q>"Just...moving in.  Hopefully, I didn't make too much noise with the truck. I tried to park as far away as possible, but..."</q> *He trailed off, his voice laced with anxiety.  He was already anticipating complaints, already bracing himself for the inevitable conflict.*
